Problem Statement
Problem: Algorithms - 43
Let S ⊆Rn. Define the polar set S◦by S◦:= {y ∈Rn | yTx ≤1 for every x ∈S}. Prove
that if S is a polyhedron, then S◦is necessarily a polyhedron as well.

0002 | **Solution:**
0003 | We will prove that if S ⊆Rn is a polyhedron, then its polar set S◦is also a polyhedron.
0004 | **Definitions and Preliminaries:** 1. A **polyhedron** is the intersection of finitely
0005 | many half-spaces, i.e., it can be written as S = {x ∈Rn | Ax ≤b} for some matrix
0006 | A ∈Rm×n and vector b ∈Rm. 2. The **polar set** of S is defined as S◦= {y ∈Rn | yTx ≤
0007 | 1 for all x ∈S}.
0008 | **Proof:**
0009 | Assume S is a polyhedron given by:
0010 | S = {x ∈Rn | Ax ≤b},
0011 | where A ∈Rm×n and b ∈Rm.
0012 | We want to show that S◦is also a polyhedron. By definition:
0013 | S◦= {y ∈Rn | yTx ≤1 for all x such that Ax ≤b}.
0014 | Using duality, the condition yTx ≤1 for all x satisfying Ax ≤b can be rephrased using
0015 | Farkas’ Lemma or linear programming duality. Specifically, yTx ≤1 for all x with Ax ≤b
0016 | holds if and only if there exists a non-negative vector λ ∈Rm
0017 | + such that:
0018 | ATλ = y
0019 | and
0020 | bTλ ≤1.
0021 | Thus, we can express S◦as:
0022 | S◦= {y ∈Rn | ∃λ ≥0 such that ATλ = y, bTλ ≤1}.
0023 | This is the projection onto the y-variables of the polyhedron defined by:
0024 | {(y, λ) ∈Rn × Rm | ATλ = y, bTλ ≤1, λ ≥0}.
0025 | Since projections of polyhedra are polyhedra (by the Fourier-Motzkin elimination process
0026 | or the Minkowski-Weyl theorem), it follows that S◦is a polyhedron.
0027 | Alternatively, we can write S◦explicitly as the intersection of half-spaces derived from
0028 | the inequalities defining S. For each row aT
0029 | i of A, the condition aT
0030 | i x ≤bi implies that for
0031 | y ∈S◦, we must have yTx ≤1 for all x satisfying aT
0032 | i x ≤bi.
0033 | If bi > 0, the maximum of yTx subject to aT
0034 | i x ≤bi is yT ai
0035 | bi
0036 | (achieved at x = ai
0037 | bi ), so we
0038 | must have yT ai

0042 | i x ≤0 must hold for all x ∈S, and yTx ≤1 for all such x
0043 | implies y must be in the recession cone of S, i.e., yTx ≤0 for all x with aT
0044 | i x ≤0. This is
0045 | equivalent to y being a non-negative multiple of ai, i.e., y = λai for some λ ≥0.
0046 | Combining these observations, S◦can be written as:
0047 | S◦= {y ∈Rn | yTai ≤bi for all i with bi > 0}∩{y ∈Rn | y = λai, λ ≥0 for all i with bi = 0}.
0048 | This is a finite intersection of half-spaces and lines (which can also be expressed as half-
0049 | spaces), hence S◦is a polyhedron.
0050 | **Conclusion:**
0051 | We have shown that the polar set S◦of a polyhedron S is itself a polyhedron, either by
0052 | duality arguments or by explicitly constructing its half-space representation.
